title: Capcom Cancelled a Nearly Finished Resident Evil for Game Boy Color
hook: Capcom shelved a Game Boy Color port of the first Resident Evil in 2000 when it was nearly done. Fans paid $2,000 in 2012 to get the prototypes released. Would you have played Resident Evil on a Game Boy?
script: Did you know a Game Boy Color version of the first Resident Evil was almost finished when Capcom killed it? In 1999, Capcom showed off a handheld port of the original game, built by a London studio called HotGen. It was aimed at Christmas of that year, then slipped into early 2000. Then in early 2000, Capcom cancelled it outright. The company said it was not confident the product would make both consumers and Capcom happy. The developers later said the build was close to complete when the call came. Capcom put out Resident Evil Gaiden on the Game Boy Color instead, a top down spin off made by a different British studio. Then in 2012, a collector offered to release two prototype cartridges if fans raised 2,000 dollars. They hit the goal within about a week, and the roms went public that February. One build was reportedly around 90 percent complete. And in December 2025, a near final build surfaced online, which one of its programmers put at about 98 percent done. So the game Capcom shelved is now playable more than 25 years later. Would you have played Resident Evil on a Game Boy? Follow for more gaming history.
